whats_working: Clear section grouping (Appearance / Text & reading / Account) with uppercase eyebrows and card containers reads well in all four theme+device combinations.
Selected state is unambiguous: theme and text-size options use primary border + primarySoft fill + primary-colored icon/label, satisfying Norman:Feedback and avoiding color-only signaling.
Sign out uses the danger token treatment (dangerSoft fill + danger border/text) consistently in light and dark, correctly signposting a destructive action without shouting.
Account guidance ('password managed by your program administrator') sets expectations up front, a good conceptual-model touch.
Text-size preview 'A' glyphs render at their actual sample sizes, giving an honest what-you-see affordance.

findings.title: iPad/Android-tablet Settings stretches to contentMaxWidth (1040–1200) instead of readableMaxWidth 760
findings.evidence: ipad/light/16-settings.png and android-tablet/light/16-settings.png: the Account card's Name/value and Email/value pairs sit at opposite screen edges with a vast empty gutter between them, and the Sign out button spans nearly the full ~1000pt width. Pack line 115 calls getResponsiveContentContainerStyle(layout, {...}) with no maxWidth override, so it defaults to layout.contentMaxWidth (NARROW/WIDE_TABLET_CONTENT_MAX_WIDTH 1040–1200 in responsive-layout-tokens.ts lines 777-778). CORE states Settings is content-light and should cap at readableMaxWidth 760.
findings.why: Wide label/value rows force the eye to travel across a large empty span to associate a label with its value, and a full-width destructive Sign out button on tablet reads as an unbalanced, scaled-up phone layout rather than an adapted large-canvas design.
findings.fix: Pass maxWidth: layout.formMaxWidth (600) or a readable 760 to getResponsiveContentContainerStyle, e.g. getResponsiveContentContainerStyle(layout, { bottomPadding: insets.bottom + 32, gap: 28, maxWidth: 760 }); this centers the column and tightens the Account rows.

findings.title: Theme and text-size option buttons use radii.lg (12) instead of radii.button (10)
findings.affected: app/settings.tsx theme options (line 134) and text-size options (line 185)
findings.evidence: Pack line 134 `rounded={radii.lg}` on the theme Button and line 185 `rounded={radii.lg}` on the text-size Button. CORE SHAPE rule: interactive buttons and step pills use radii.button=10; lg (14 per CORE / 12 per design-system.ts) is for cards. The back button (line 95) and Sign out (line 262) correctly use radii.button.
findings.why: These are tappable selectable controls, so per the shared radius contract they should carry the button radius; mixing lg on some buttons and button on others is a subtle within-screen inconsistency.
findings.fix: Change `rounded={radii.lg}` to `rounded={radii.button}` on both option Buttons (lines 134 and 185).

findings.title: Sign out and option rows hand-roll tamagui Button styling instead of the shared AppButton primitive
findings.affected: app/settings.tsx Sign out Button (lines 260-282) and header back Button (91-104)
findings.evidence: design_system_components_used lists only ScaledParagraph, ScaledText — no AppButton. CORE ships AppButton(primary|secondary|ghost|danger + loading + disabled). The Sign out control inlines danger colors, border, height 52, radius, and pressStyle by hand (lines 260-282) rather than <AppButton variant="danger">, and thus has no loading/disabled state during the async logout() (line 268 fires `void logout()` with no visible feedback).
findings.why: Re-implementing a danger button inline drifts from the shared component (padding, press feedback, disabled semantics) and, more importantly, the raw Button gives no pressed/in-flight feedback while sign-out runs, violating Nielsen H1 visibility of system status.
findings.fix: Replace the inline Sign out Button with <AppButton variant="danger" loading={isSigningOut} onPress={...}> and track a local isSigningOut flag around logout(); use AppButton (ghost/secondary) for the back control too.

findings.title: Dyslexia-friendly OFF switch track is nearly invisible on dark surface
findings.evidence: iphone/dark/20-settings.png and android-tablet/dark/16-settings.png: the OFF switch track blends almost completely into the card surface; the pill outline is barely discernible. Pack line 234 sets trackColor false to colors.mutedSurface (#2B2D26) which sits on surface #1E201C — an extremely low luminance delta, and the thumb uses colors.surface (line 235) which is also near-identical to the track.
findings.why: In dark mode the toggle's off affordance is hard to perceive, so users may not realize the control is interactive or what its current state is (Norman: affordance/signifier failure); the thumb/track pair also lacks a clear boundary.
findings.fix: For the OFF track in dark mode use a lighter neutral (e.g. colors.border #34362E or mutedForeground-tinted) and set thumbColor to a higher-contrast value than surface (e.g. colors.foreground or a raised neutral) so the off state is visible.

findings.title: Header 'Settings' title is a fixed fontSize 22 that does not scale up on tablet
findings.evidence: ipad/light/16-settings.png: the small chevron/back header 'Settings' at ~22pt looks modest next to the very large page-body 'Settings' heading, and against the tablet ×1.3 typography baseline (TABLET_TYPOGRAPHY_BASE_SCALE, responsive-layout-tokens.ts line 790) the header eyebrow/title do not visibly grow. The hardcoded 22 is not derived from a responsive token.
findings.why: A fixed header size on the large canvas slightly undercuts the visual hierarchy the tablet baseline intends; it is cosmetic but contributes to the scaled-up-phone feel of the top bar.
findings.fix: Drive the header title size from the layout token (e.g. layout.isTablet ? 26 : 22) or a shared heading size, letting ScaledText continue to apply the user font scale.
